channel.title: The Wake Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wake Weekly (wakeweekly.com)

item.title: Bridle named assistant county manager for Franklin County
item.description: Franklin County names veteran local government official David Bridle as assistant county manager, succeeding Ryan Preble; he starts March 30.

item.title: Habitat for Humanity partners with elected officials to build affordab...
item.description: Habitat for Humanity of Wake County and local officials marked the nonprofit’s 1,000th affordable home build in Garner, spotlighting the region’s housing crisis and push for policy change.

item.title: Wake County commissioners approve plans to replace EMS station in nort...
item.description: Wake County OKs plan to replace 1989 EMS Station 5 in north Raleigh with larger, eco-friendly facility featuring more ambulance space and expanded staff areas by 2028.

item.title: Wake County names Ruffin Hall as deputy county manager
item.description: Wake County has named former Raleigh city manager and Dix Park Conservancy CEO Ruffin Hall as a deputy county manager, overseeing EMS, fire, forensic services and emergency communications.

item.title: School recess was the best
item.description: Columnist Rix Quinn recalls chaotic elementary school recess — lunchroom rules, bathroom pranks, bird-call hoaxes — and how those playful urges still surface after lunch today.

item.title: NC utilities commissioner warns against ‘throwing good money after bad...
item.description: NC utilities commissioner Donald van der Vaart likens Duke Energy's solar buildout to buying seven unreliable cars and warns the added costs may fall on ratepayers.

item.title: Rural residents face the biggest risks from postal delays
item.description: USPS cuts to evening mail pickups at rural post offices mean ballots, tax returns and bill payments may be postmarked late, risking voter disenfranchisement and higher costs for seniors without broadband.

item.title: This year, the case against lawns gets even stronger
item.description: Rising fuel and fertilizer costs tied to Middle East conflict sharpen the case against traditional lawns, highlighting their time, financial, legal and environmental burdens compared to more natural yards.
